answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to a physical secure enclave. Joining requires remote attestation from a TEE whose manufacturer signs a device-unique key, and the ledger enforces one identity per enclave key, rejecting a second minting from the same hardware. Each identity is an island held by one attested device, so clones rising at dawn need one machine each, a linear non-shareable cost. A voyage toward many identities means buying many devices, deterring cheap minting only while device price tops a clone's marginal reward, so a wealthy attacker still wins.
